# Code spec — section fetch and convention tooling

**code spec** · **Status: DRAFT** — awaiting Dean's finalization. First spec written in the
atomic-step shape defined by
[`atomic-step-protocol-design.md`](atomic-step-protocol-design.md), so it doubles as the template.

---

## Reading Protocol

Read this protocol, `## Intent`, and `## Step index`. Then start at your assigned step and read only
that step's section — by anchor link, or by extracting from its heading to the next heading of the same
or higher level. Do not read the whole document. There are no line numbers, and
`scripts/toc-refresh.sh` must **not** be run against this file: it would add line ranges that this shape
deliberately retires.

---

## Intent

**intent** — Build the four tools that make heading-addressed fetching real: `sec`, `conv`, `conv-list`,
`conv-lint`. Everything else in the migration depends on them, and nothing else in the migration can
start until they exist.

**current call stack** — Nothing. Sections are addressed today by `Read <file> offset:N limit:M`, using
line ranges kept in each document's TOC and regenerated by `scripts/toc-refresh.sh`. Line numbers are a
global index over a mutable document, so any insertion invalidates every range below it and a stale range
mis-points silently. `plans/conventions/` does not exist; `session/CONVENTIONS.md` still cites a
`plans/rules/INDEX.md` that never did.

**planned call stack** —

```
a caller wants one section        →  sec <file> <id>...
a caller wants one convention     →  conv <name>...        (discovers the file, then extracts)
a caller wants the whole index    →  conv-list             (computed, never stored)
a gate wants structural proof     →  conv-lint             (pre-commit, and inside plan-lint later)
```

**new components** — four scripts and a test harness. No production code, no Go, nothing that ships in a
PR. All of it lands on an orphan `plans-tooling` branch and is copied into `plans/` later as one
deliberate kickoff commit.

---

## Prerequisites — not steps

Done by whoever launches the coder, not by the coder (it cannot create the worktree it starts in):

```
git -C repo worktree add ../plans-tooling --orphan plans-tooling
```

An **orphan** branch on purpose: the worktree then contains only this work, so the coder physically
cannot reach `CURRENT.md`, `planning/`, or `session/`. Confinement by layout rather than by rule. It may
read `../plans/` for realistic fixtures.

**Gates for this spec** — the usual ones do not apply. There is no Go, so no `make test`, no `gofmt`, no
`go build`. The plans lineage takes **no DCO sign-off**. What replaces them, per step:

- `bash -n <script>` — parses
- `shellcheck <script>` if installed; note its absence rather than skipping silently
- the golden tests from S1
- every documented error path exits non-zero with a message on **stderr**

**Do not push.** Local commits only, on `plans-tooling`.

---

## Step index

Briefs only. Details are below the divide, fetched at execution.

**S1 — Test harness and fixtures.** Nothing can be verified without goldens, so this comes first.
Fixtures must include the nasty cases deliberately: nested heading levels, a `####` subsection inside a
section, two headings that slug identically, a section at end-of-file. Decision: goldens are committed
expected-output files compared with `diff`, not assertions in code — a diff shows *what* changed.

**S2 — `sec`, single id.** The core extractor: from the matching heading to the next heading of the same
or higher level. Hazard already known from `session-extract.sh`: a `##` inserted inside a section
truncates it and a `####` gets absorbed, so the level arithmetic is the whole correctness question.

**S3 — `sec`, multiple ids and error paths.** Multiple sections in one call is what makes a step's whole
convention set a single fetch, so it is not a nicety. Unresolved and *ambiguous* ids must both fail
loudly and differently — an ambiguous id must never be resolved by picking the first match.

**S4 — `conv`.** Name-to-file discovery by scanning `conventions/*.md`, then delegate to `sec`. Rationale
for no index file: the marker carries the name, so a scan cannot go stale where an index can.

**S5 — `conv-list`.** The computed index — name plus description per convention. This is what replaces
`rules/INDEX.md`, and computing it is why no index file is needed.

**S6 — `conv-lint`.** Structural proof: marker format, name uniqueness, required fields, heading levels
that would truncate, referenced paths that no longer resolve. Runs standalone, in a pre-commit hook, and
inside `plan-lint` later.

**S7 — Usage documentation.** A README in the worktree covering all four tools, written against the
finished behavior rather than the intent.

## S1 — Test harness and fixtures

**brief** — Goldens before tools: every later step is verified by `diff` against committed expected
output. Fixtures carry the hard cases from the start so S2's level arithmetic is exercised immediately
rather than discovered later.

**scope** — `tests/`

**do**
1. `tests/fixtures/doc-a.md` — sections at `##` and `###`, one `##` section containing a `####`
   subsection, one section that runs to end-of-file, and **two headings whose slugs collide**.
2. `tests/fixtures/conventions/commits.md` and `tests/fixtures/conventions/git.md` — several
   `### convention: <name>` sections each, with `description`/`scope`/`trigger`/`status`/`origin` field
   lines. Include one convention with `status: probation`.
3. `tests/expected/` — one file per case, named `<tool>-<case>.out`.
4. `tests/run.sh` — runs each case, diffs against its expected file, prints one line per case, exits
   non-zero if any differ. Support `--update` to regenerate goldens deliberately.

**conventions** — none (see § Intent). Inline rules: `set -uo pipefail`; no `sed -i`; every failure path
prints to stderr and exits non-zero.

**verify** — `bash -n tests/run.sh`; `./tests/run.sh` runs and reports zero cases (no tools yet) rather
than erroring; `./tests/run.sh --update` is idempotent on a second run.

**done_when** — `tests/run.sh` exits 0 with no cases registered, and the fixture files exist with the
five hard cases present.

**on_fail** — halt.

**record** — fixture list and which hard case each covers.

[↑ Step index](#step-index)

## S2 — `sec`, single id

**brief** — Extract one section, addressed by heading. An id resolves if it matches the heading's GitHub
anchor slug (lowercased, spaces to hyphens, punctuation dropped) **or** the exact heading text. Output
includes the heading itself.

**scope** — `scripts/sec.sh`, `tests/`

**do**
1. Accept `sec <file> <id>`.
2. Find the heading whose slug or exact text matches. Record its level as the count of leading `#`.
3. Emit from that heading up to — not including — the next heading whose level is **less than or equal
   to** it. A deeper heading (`####` under `###`) stays inside; a same-or-shallower one ends the section.
4. A section that runs to end-of-file ends there.
5. Register cases in `tests/run.sh` for: `##` section, `###` section, section containing a deeper
   subsection, section at end-of-file.

**conventions** — none. Inline: unresolved id → exit non-zero with the id named on stderr, never empty
output on success-looking exit 0. That distinction is the whole point — an empty section and a bad id
must not look alike.

**verify** — `bash -n`; `shellcheck` if present; `./tests/run.sh` green for the four new cases;
`./scripts/sec.sh tests/fixtures/doc-a.md no-such-id; echo $?` prints non-zero.

**done_when** — the four cases pass by `diff`, and a bad id exits non-zero with a stderr message.

**on_fail** — halt. Do not "fix" a golden to match the tool without saying so in `record`.

**record** — the level rule as implemented, and any fixture case whose expected output surprised you.

[↑ Step index](#step-index)

## S3 — `sec`, multiple ids and error paths

**brief** — Multiple ids in one invocation is what lets a step fetch its whole convention set in a single
round trip. Ambiguity must be an error, not a choice.

**scope** — `scripts/sec.sh`, `tests/`

**do**
1. Accept `sec <file> <id>...`; emit sections in the order the ids were given, separated by a blank line.
2. If any id is unresolved: report **every** unresolved id, then exit non-zero. Do not emit partial
   output as if it succeeded.
3. If an id matches more than one heading: exit non-zero naming the collision. **Never pick the first.**
   The colliding-slug fixture from S1 covers this.
4. Add cases: two ids, three ids, one bad among two good, the ambiguous id.

**conventions** — none. Inline: distinct exit codes for distinct failures (usage vs unresolved vs
ambiguous), documented in the header comment.

**verify** — `./tests/run.sh` green; the bad-among-good case exits non-zero **and** emits no partial
section; the ambiguous case names both headings.

**done_when** — all multi-id cases pass, and both failure modes are distinguishable by exit code.

**on_fail** — halt.

**record** — the exit-code table.

[↑ Step index](#step-index)

## S4 — `conv`

**brief** — `conv <name>...` finds which topic file holds each named convention, then extracts it. No
index file: the `### convention: <name>` marker carries the name, so a scan cannot go stale.

**scope** — `scripts/conv.sh`, `tests/`

**do**
1. Accept `conv <name>...`, and a `--dir` override defaulting to `conventions/`.
2. For each name, scan `<dir>/*.md` for a heading matching `### convention: <name>` exactly.
3. Extract via `scripts/sec.sh` — do not reimplement the extraction.
4. A name found in **two** files exits non-zero naming both. Uniqueness is `conv-lint`'s job to report,
   but `conv` must not silently choose.
5. An unresolved name exits non-zero; if it is cheap, list near-miss names to catch typos.
6. Cases: one name, three names in one call, unknown name, duplicated name across two files.

**conventions** — none. Inline: reuse `sec.sh` rather than duplicating the level arithmetic — two copies
would drift and the drift would be silent.

**verify** — `./tests/run.sh` green; three names in one call produce three sections in argument order;
unknown name exits non-zero.

**done_when** — all four cases pass and `conv.sh` contains no extraction logic of its own.

**on_fail** — halt.

**record** — whether near-miss suggestions were implemented, and why if not.

[↑ Step index](#step-index)

## S5 — `conv-list`

**brief** — The computed index: every convention's name and description, so a spec owner can find the
right one when writing a step manifest. Computing it is the reason no index file exists.

**scope** — `scripts/conv-list.sh`, `tests/`

**do**
1. Scan `conventions/*.md` for every `### convention: <name>`, and read the `description`, `status` and
   `scope` field lines that follow it.
2. Print one line per convention: name, status, description. Stable order — sort by name so the output
   diffs cleanly.
3. Mark `status: probation` visibly; a probation convention is still binding and must not read as
   disabled.
4. A convention missing its `description` is listed with a visible placeholder, not skipped. Silence
   would hide exactly what `conv-lint` needs to catch.
5. Cases: the two fixture topic files; one convention lacking a description.

**conventions** — none. Inline: stable sort so goldens are deterministic.

**verify** — `./tests/run.sh` green; output order identical across two runs.

**done_when** — cases pass, probation is visibly marked, a description-less convention still appears.

**on_fail** — halt.

**record** — the output format, since `plan-lint` and the role kernels will both read it later.

[↑ Step index](#step-index)

## S6 — `conv-lint`

**brief** — Turns "nothing is malformed" into a machine-checked property. Every check here exists because
its absence fails **silently**: a malformed marker makes a convention unfetchable, and the coder then
halts as though it never existed.

**scope** — `scripts/conv-lint.sh`, `tests/`

**do**
1. Marker format — `### convention: <slug>` with `slug` matching `[a-z0-9-]+`.
2. Name uniqueness across all topic files.
3. Required fields present per convention: `description`, `scope`, `trigger`, `status`, `origin`.
4. `status` is `active` or `probation`, nothing else.
5. Heading-level sanity — no `##` inside a convention section, which would truncate it at extraction.
6. Referenced paths in a convention body resolve on disk.
7. Report **every** violation with file and name, then exit non-zero. Clean input: silent, exit 0.
8. Cases: one clean run; one fixture per violation class under `tests/fixtures/bad/`.

**conventions** — none. Inline: report all violations, never stop at the first — a linter that reports one
of six problems costs six runs.

**verify** — `./tests/run.sh` green; clean fixtures produce empty output and exit 0; each bad fixture
exits non-zero naming its own violation.

**done_when** — every check has a passing case and a failing case. A check with no failing fixture is not
proven to work.

**on_fail** — halt.

**record** — the check list with its exit codes, and any check deferred with the reason.

[↑ Step index](#step-index)

## S7 — Usage documentation

**brief** — A README covering all four tools, written against finished behavior. Not a design document:
it says what the tools do, not why they exist.

**scope** — `README.md`

**do**
1. One section per tool: synopsis, arguments, exit codes, one worked example run against the fixtures.
2. State the two addressing rules that are easy to get wrong: ids are heading slugs or exact heading
   text, and a section ends at the next heading of the same or higher level.
3. State that no tool takes or emits line numbers.
4. Note that these tools are copied into `plans/scripts/` at kickoff, not pushed from here.

**conventions** — none. Inline: no plans-branch identifiers in this README — it travels with the code.

**verify** — every example in the README is run and its output matches what is shown. A README example
that was never executed is a defect.

**done_when** — all four tools documented, every example verified by running it.

**on_fail** — halt.

**record** — anything the documentation pass revealed about the tools themselves; writing usage docs
routinely exposes bad interfaces.

## After the steps — not the coder's work

Kickoff is Dean's single deliberate action: copy `scripts/` and `tests/` into `plans/` and commit once.
The development history stays on `plans-tooling`, which is archived rather than merged.

Then, in order: `conv-new` / `conv-edit` / `conv-rename` and the pre-commit hook (M1.0), the `r-*` role
skills (M1.1), the harvest (M1.2), the coverage audit (M1.3).

`conv-rename` is deliberately absent from this spec: citation rewriting has nothing to scan until step
manifests exist. `plan-lint` likewise — it would validate a document shape nothing uses yet.
